posts.author: The_Downward_Samsara
posts.body:
I'm
The_Downward_Samsara
(a play on the Buddhist concept of rebirth and the NIИ album- yeah,
that
one). I live on the West Coast of the US, in fact not too far south from where Cyberpunk's
Night City
is situated.
I've been a part of the RM community off and on since RM2K/2K3 on the GameFAQs boards, XP over at RMN (
RIP?
), and Recently at the RPG Maker sub on Reddit. I'm gearing up to get into MZ as soon as there's a sale, hopefully sometime in February. I remember the old days and players like Don Miguel, RPG Advocate, GDKT/Alex Trapper, SSB5, Fwuffy Kitty, MagusFire, Pyropinoy, Nameless, Danny Ledonne, and many, many others.
Most of my experience has been limited to learning the basic commands, rather than scripts or plugins. Though I have a graphics and CG background, pixel work is not exactly my strong suit. I've also never finished a project, sadly. I've lost plenty of projects from hardware failures over the past 25 years. Some of the things I've learned a lot about included interactive map screens, day/night systems, complex conversation branches, animated game over screens (
ahead of its time for 2K
), trophy walls, custom menus and character creation systems.
I had plenty of my own stories, but a good portion of my learning experience was replicating other games to see how they did it. One project was notable for combining FF1-3 into one big remake using FF6 sprites, but I gave it up soon after Dawn of Souls was announced. I also had a Zelda 1+2 remake using edited RTP and a project called
Tears of the Dragon
, which was essentially a Pool of Radiance ripoff.
For a while I was also doing custom title screens for a few devs. I don't know if any of their projects were completed. I later worked on more original projects, Including "
Fallout: Genetic Terror
" which was set in the Great Lakes area, "
Xenocop
" a sci-fi game about an alien cop, and an unnamed space trading/piracy side scroller RPG that was Firefly-esque(
?
).
I've been into storytelling and RPGs ever since I was a kid, and I've always wanted to publish a game of my own that would be remembered. I have an ex who got her art in a major AAA title (it rhymes with 'Sims2') and it absolutely irks me that it technically makes her closer to a dev than I am! My latest idea is for a game in a cyberpunk setting with zombie-like creatures running amok. I'm having good feelings about this one.
A little about me:
I also like Anime, Manga, Film, Electronic Music, and Cyberpunk or Fantasy Novels.
Favorite films include: It's Such A Beautiful Day, Redline, Poolboy: Drowning Out The Fury, Big Man Japan, and Love Exposure. Clear your calendar for that last one,
it's 4 hours long
.
I've seen at least 3,000 movies. I can't tell you about any of them because it's all a blur at this point. Also, not all of them were great. Don't even ask me about Andy Warhol's Bad.
I like cats and dogs equally. The bigger the dog, the bigger the cuddles. My cat has a strict boundary about cuddles.
I don't follow sports unless it's sumo wrestling, rodeo clown competitions, or slap fights.
College radio was a  musical awakening for me in the late 80's and there isn't much in the way of music that offends me, other than the hot garbage that Nashville has been vomiting up the past decade.
If I had to live with only eating 3 foods, they'd be Unagi Nigiri, Tonkatsu Ramen, and Sicilian-Style Pepperoni Pizza.
Some spicy takes:
Kaneda's bike was not electric, it was a hybrid.
Amazon did in fact ruin The Wheel Of Time. Rafe was a huge mistake. In general.
People should be required to have a license in order to have kids.
Mars is a stupid place to go when we haven't even put our manufacturing on the moon yet.
Stopping at an empty roundabout = Straight to jail.
So anyways, thought I'd introduce myself. If anyone wants to see screenies of my horribly outdated 2K3 crap let me know.

posts.author: Ulqiuo
posts.body:
Howdy The_Downward_Samsara! Nice to get to know you. Probably the most detailed and informative welcome I've read since I joined a week or two ago haha! I hope you fit in comfortably.
It's great to hear you've got prior experience (even if it's on an older engine) - the more the merrier. You'll possibly find that the future iterations, whilst being upgraded and snazzier, run quite similarly. Great if you want to jump straight in!
I still remember watching a playthrough of the every-famous Ib from a popular youtuber aaages ago, t'was my inspiration for coming here, albeit very late.
If I may introduce a caveat - if you fancy learning the plugins and scripts part of RPG Maker MZ I recommend RPG Maker MV. It's only one version backwards but it goes down to as little as £12 when on sale, and the plugins are more plentiful, and not to mention cheaper (or even free) to get ahold of. I've seen a full plugin bundle from Yanfly (popular plugin maker in the day) go for around $30 standard, but can be gotten for under a tenner I believe when it does go on sale. It contains a heckuva lot of stuff! ...Not that I want to influence your decision at all haha, just food for thought.
Ditto on the never-finished-a-project part too, but we'll get there one day so long as we don't give up eh? Best of luck to you! Looking forward to what you can create, especially story-wise!

posts.author: The_Downward_Samsara
posts.body:
Thanks for the warm welcome!
Actually due to the sales, I ended up with MZ, MV, VXA, 2K3, and 2K, combined with XP, I'm pretty much set! Now to wade through too many plugins...

posts.author: Ulqiuo
posts.body: Hahah! That's a fantastic selection, to be fair. I hear there's still major usage for the XP version, as well as VX Ace. Have fun!
